answer.rationale: With expiry in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% with no buffer, defer_decision risks a line stop and switch_primary_vendor imports migration risk exactly when there is no slack; memory_c2's low-cost switch succeeded last year under unknown buffer conditions, so I want it verified before relying on or rejecting it. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, which weakens a straight memory_c4 benchmark play, so the intended path is negotiate_terms structured as a multi-year/volume commitment (memory_c6) to reach toward the 18% mandate while preserving the stable integration that memory_c1 shows has protected deliveries. This targets TCO via unit-cost and terms rather than a risky supply-base change. Risk is flagged because a failed negotiation near expiry could force a distressed renewal; uncertainty is preserved pending the archive check on c2 and the incumbent's response to a term-based rather than price-reopen ask.
